target_zone_range.note: BONAP was reviewed as the primary county-level range authority. The >=3-county project threshold is independently supported by locality/specimen documentation for Hays, Travis, and Williamson counties. Additional counties from the prior working record are retained separately until they are individually rechecked.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial herb, usually about 10–50 cm tall; several stems arise from a thick rootstalk, with stems ascending to decumbent and often branched from the base.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Ovate to lanceolate leaves on petioles; margins often conspicuously wavy/undulate; leaf surfaces can be short-hairy, especially along veins.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Lateral/axillary umbels on upper nodes; commonly one cluster per node and often short-peduncled.
morphology_keys.flower_color: Greenish-white to yellowish, sometimes with cream or pink tones in the corona.
morphology_keys.gynostegium_detail: Very long, slender corona hoods extend above the stigmatic head and flare or bow outward near their tips; internal horns are present. This hood shape is exceptionally diagnostic.
best_field_traits: At flower level, the very long slender corona hoods rise above the central gynostegium—an unusually strong Texas milkweed character.
Opposite broad leaves with conspicuously wavy margins.
Low, several-stemmed habit with lateral/axillary umbels.
Use a macro view to separate the corona hoods, central gynostegium, and reflexed corolla parts.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: Joey Santore's South Texas macro photographs make the decisive floral anatomy especially easy to learn: long narrow hoods/corona surrounding the central gynostegium, with the reflexed corolla visible below.

fastest_traits: Opposite broad leaves with conspicuously wavy margins
Lateral flower clusters rather than only a single terminal cluster
Very long slender hoods projecting well above the central column
field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: TPWD describes the long slender hoods as unique among Texas milkweeds and sufficient to distinguish Zizotes milkweed from the other species in the guide.

look_alikes.distinction: Check the corona. A. oenotheroides has unusually elongated tubular hoods that extend distinctly above the stigmatic head.

ecological_notes.habitat: Rocky calcareous limestone and igneous soils in the Edwards Plateau, High Plains, Rolling Plains, Trans-Pecos and Tamaulipan regions; also tight sandy clay and coastal dunes.
ecological_notes.central_texas_note: Documented as a naturally occurring milkweed in Hays County and Travis County and as part of the Williamson County flora.
ecological_notes.drought_response: Can persist through dry periods and rapidly leaf out and flower after rainfall.
ecological_notes.host_status: Native Asclepias and a larval host used by monarchs; also provides floral resources for pollinators.
